
DELETE-WORK-UNIT
Delete a work unit and all its data

WHEN TO USE
  Use this command to permanently remove a work unit from the project. This deletes all associated data including Example Mapping results, dependencies, and state tracking. Use with caution as this operation cannot be undone.

PREREQUISITES
  • Work unit must exist in spec/work-units.json

USAGE
  fspec delete-work-unit <workUnitId> [options]

ARGUMENTS
  <workUnitId> (required)
    Work unit ID to delete (e.g., AUTH-001)

OPTIONS
  --force
    Force deletion without validation checks
  --skip-confirmation
    Skip confirmation prompt (use in scripts)
  --cascade-dependencies
    Remove all dependency relationships before deleting

COMMON PATTERNS
  • Safe Deletion with Checks
    Example: # Check what will be deleted
fspec show-work-unit AUTH-999
fspec dependencies AUTH-999

# Delete with cascading
fspec delete-work-unit AUTH-999 --cascade-dependencies
    undefined

  • Scripted Deletion
    Example: # Delete in automated scripts
fspec delete-work-unit AUTH-999 --skip-confirmation --cascade-dependencies
    undefined


TYPICAL WORKFLOW
  1. Verify work unit: fspec show-work-unit <id> → 2. Check dependencies: fspec dependencies <id> → 3. Delete: fspec delete-work-unit <id> --cascade-dependencies

EXAMPLES
  1. Delete work unit (with confirmation)
  $ fspec delete-work-unit AUTH-999
  Are you sure? (y/N): y
✓ Work unit AUTH-999 deleted successfully

  2. Delete without confirmation
  $ fspec delete-work-unit AUTH-999 --skip-confirmation
  ✓ Work unit AUTH-999 deleted successfully

  3. Delete and remove all dependencies
  $ fspec delete-work-unit AUTH-999 --cascade-dependencies
  ✓ Work unit AUTH-999 deleted successfully
⚠ This work unit blocks 2 work unit(s): API-001, UI-001

  4. Force delete without any checks
  $ fspec delete-work-unit AUTH-999 --force --skip-confirmation
  ✓ Work unit AUTH-999 deleted successfully

COMMON ERRORS
  ✗ Error: Work unit AUTH-999 does not exist
    Fix: Verify work unit ID with: fspec list-work-units

  ✗ Error: Cannot delete work unit with children: AUTH-002, AUTH-003. Delete children first or remove parent relationship.
    Fix: Either delete child work units first, or remove the parent relationship from children

  ✗ Error: Work unit AUTH-001 has dependencies. Use --cascade-dependencies flag to remove dependencies and delete.
    Fix: Add --cascade-dependencies flag to remove all dependency relationships before deletion

RELATED COMMANDS
  fspec list-work-units
  fspec create-story
  fspec create-bug
  fspec create-task
  fspec show-work-unit
  fspec dependencies

NOTES
  • Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone
  • Deletes all Example Mapping data associated with the work unit
  • Removes work unit from all state arrays (backlog, specifying, etc.)
  • Removes work unit from parent's children array if it has a parent
  • Cannot delete work units that have children (delete children first)
  • Use --cascade-dependencies to remove all dependency relationships automatically
  • --force flag bypasses validation checks (use with caution)
  • --skip-confirmation is useful for automated scripts
